bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to veterans affairs; expanding eligibility for certain benefits to former members of the National Guard or reservists; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 197.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[197.449] FORMER MEMBERS OF NATIONAL GUARD OR RESERVISTS.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Time of hostilities" has the meaning given in section 197.791, subdivision 1, paragraph (g).

(c) "Eligible veteran" means a person who:

(1) resides in this state;

(2) during a time of hostilities:

(i) served as a member of the state's National Guard; or

(ii) served in a reserve component of the United States armed forces;

(3) completed their applicable military service obligation as defined by United States Code, title 10, section 651; and

(4) received an honorable discharge.

Subd. 2.

Eligibility for benefits and privileges.

The following statutory benefits and privileges available to a veteran, as defined in section 197.447, are also available to an eligible veteran: section 197.23 (purchase of grave markers); section 197.231 (honor guards); section 197.236 (state veterans cemeteries); section 197.455 (veterans preference); section 197.4551 (permissive preference for veterans in private employment); section 197.63 (vital records, certified copies); section 197.65 (renewal of professional license, motor vehicle registration, and driver's license); and section 197.987 (honor and remember flag).
